what_this_is: O16/O17 measured on a 4K->1080x1920 downscale, the case R5.5 nominates as where a resampling difference should appear. Candidate vs the SAME filter graph at slow/crf12, so the encode is isolated. Two sources, deliberately unlike each other.

sources.A_testsrc2: synthetic pattern, hard edges, high contrast
sources.B_noise_bars: SMPTE bars + temporal/uniform noise + slight blur; grain and gradients

preset_decision.why: The two sources CONTRADICT each other. On A every slower preset beat veryfast (+0.677..+1.137 VMAF); on B every slower preset was worse (-0.185..-0.586 VMAF). R4.3 permits a default change only if the measurement shows a fidelity improvement, and this does not show one. What slower presets DID reliably produce was a smaller file at equal CRF (-1.61..-1.83 MB on B), which is what x264 presets actually trade -- compression efficiency, not fidelity. Anyone optimising for upload size rather than encode time has a real reason to move this; anyone expecting a quality gain does not.
preset_decision.time_cost_if_changed: faster x1.05-x1.19, fast x1.28-x1.38, medium x1.29-x1.51, paid three times per clip

scaler_decision.why: lanczos -- the algorithm usually recommended for downscaling -- is WITHIN NOISE of bicubic: VMAF -0.071, SSIM +0.000896, PSNR +0.03. R5.6 is explicit that a measurement which cannot distinguish the candidates means keeping the default and recording the finding. bicubic is also swscale's own default, so no pixels move and no fixture needed re-freezing.
scaler_decision.one_clear_result: bilinear is measurably worse (VMAF -2.796) and is what several ffmpeg wrappers pass by default, so it is worth knowing not to.
scaler_decision.metric_disagreement: neighbor scored the BEST VMAF (+0.749) while losing 1.02 dB PSNR and 0.005 SSIM. That is VMAF being fooled by nearest-neighbour's false sharpening. It is the clearest evidence in this repo that a single metric is not a verdict -- worth remembering given M9 exists precisely to let numbers settle arguments.

audio_o20.why: NOT MEASURED. M9's three metrics are all image metrics, so nothing here can compare 128k against 192k. R7.5 wants a measurement before the default moves; the setting is the honest deliverable and the default is not a claim.

caveat: Two synthetic sources. Neither is real footage, and the contradiction between them is itself the argument for not generalising from either. A bake-off on your own material would be worth more than both.
